findings.failure_path: The 'complete_locator_inventory' claim of 30/30 shifted with zero unchanged occurrences per owner cannot be confirmed from a 5-hunk packet covering a ~1240-row table. findings.smallest_fix: Attach the full-file grep of all locators into the three owner files with old/new line and shift delta per occurrence (including the unshifted below-insertion ones), so the 30-of-30 count is checkable rather than asserted.

findings.failure_path: The gated outcome is self-adjudicated: the artifact is produced by obligation-ledger.py render and the audit (2733) passes by byte-comparing the rendered index against a fresh render from the same generator plus the same unchanged mapping. Any systematic generator error (e.g. a blanket +2 for the whole owner file rather than per-occurrence recomputation) reproduces identically on both sides and exits 0. Combined with full make test and hosted CI still pending, 'audit now exits 0' is not evidence that the locators match current source.
findings.smallest_fix: Gate on an independent check that does not reuse the renderer — e.g. assert for each changed range that the current source lines equal the pre-insertion carrier text, emitted as a standalone log — and do not record a release verdict until the pending make test and hosted CI complete.

findings.failure_path: O1210 (122-123→124-125) and O1211 (123-124→125-126) are multi-line spans shifted uniformly at both endpoints. That is only correct if the 2-line insert lies strictly above the span. If any insert landed inside a span, the correct result is a widened end (start+0/end+2), not a uniform shift, and the byte-compare audit would not distinguish the two because the generator would emit the same wrong span it validated.
findings.smallest_fix: Record the absolute insertion line offsets per owner file and assert every changed span either lies wholly after them (uniform shift) or is explicitly widened.

findings.failure_path: Acceptance pins obligation-mapping.jsonl as unchanged while all locators in the reader index move by 2. If the canonical mapping stores any positional data of its own, it is now stale, and the audit described in the evidence (index byte-compare plus mapping shape/exact-carrier checks) would not surface the divergence between mapping positions and refreshed index positions.
findings.smallest_fix: State explicitly, with a field list from the mapping schema, that obligation-mapping.jsonl carries no line-position fields; if it does, regenerate them in the same partition.

concern_results.conclusion: Shift arithmetic inside the visible hunks is internally consistent: 30 changed ranges (llm 4, defect 1, testing 25), every start and end +2, duplicate references to the same old line (129→131 twice, 131→133 three times) shifted identically, and the overlapping multi-line spans 122-123→124-125 / 123-124→125-126 stay contiguous. But the packet is 5 hunks of a ~1240-row table, so the central claim under review — 'zero unchanged occurrences in each owner' from a whole-file enumeration — is unverifiable here: any row referencing skills/testing-strategy/SKILL.md, skills/llm-inference-integration/SKILL.md or skills/defect-diagnosis/SKILL.md at a line at/after the insertion point that lives outside these hunks would remain stale and invisible. The uniform +2 also silently assumes a single contiguous 2-line insert above every reference in each owner; two separate 1-line inserts would produce +1 for some locators and this diff would look identical for the ones shown. Counterexample class stands unrefuted by the packet.

No rule text, gate predicate, threshold, permission or executable is touched — only generated locator numerals — so no authority is redefined by the diff itself. The containment risk is adjudication: the gated outcome ('repo audit passes, zero unresolved') is reached by regenerating the artifact with the same generator whose output the audit byte-compares, and the evidence itself records that full make test and hosted CI are still pending. Green is asserted from a locally reproduced focused audit only; the acceptance criterion demanding a passing repository audit is therefore not independently demonstrated in this packet.
